requirements.quote:
Unidirectional streams use either the sending or receiving state
   machine, depending on the stream type and endpoint role.
requirements.condition: For a unidirectional stream, according to its type and the endpoint's role.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the applicable sending or receiving stream state-machine behavior.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply both sending and receiving state machines to the same endpoint's unidirectional stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can determine the stream direction and endpoint role, then verify that only the applicable send or receive behavior is exposed.

requirements.quote: Bidirectional streams use both state machines at both endpoints.  For
requirements.condition: For a bidirectional stream at either endpoint.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply both the sending and receiving state-machine behavior.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not model a bidirectional stream at an endpoint with only one of the sending or receiving components.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can verify that each endpoint supports both sending-side and receiving-side behavior for a bidirectional stream.

requirements.quote:
opening a stream are slightly more complex for a bidirectional stream
   because the opening of either the send or receive side causes the
   stream to open in both directions.
requirements.condition: When either the send side or receive side of a bidirectional stream opens.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the bidirectional stream as open in both directions.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not leave the opposite direction unopened after either side opens.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can trigger opening through either side independently and observe whether both directions become open.

requirements.quote:
implementation can define a different state machine as long as its
   behavior is consistent with an implementation that implements these
   states.
requirements.condition: When an implementation defines a stream state machine different from the one described in this document.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure its externally observable behavior is consistent with an implementation of the described states.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a different state machine whose behavior is inconsistent with the described state-machine behavior.
requirements.why_checkable: Conformance tests can compare the alternative machine's observable frame-sending and frame-reception reactions against those required by the described states.
